title: Real conversations
goal: Hold long, natural conversations that pull everything together: catch up with an old friend, tell a story in one breath, plan a trip and argue it out, and move smoothly between ତୁ, ତୁମେ and ଆପଣ at a family dinner.
intro:
This is where it all comes together. Real conversations don't come in neat units: you catch up with an old friend, tell what happened in long linked sentences, plan a weekend trip and argue about the destination, and then grandma walks in and the whole room shifts from ତୁ to ଆପଣ.

Two skills make the difference between correct Odia and fluent Odia. First, **linking**: Odia strings actions together with the -ଇ form and friends (ଉଠି, ଚା ପିଇ, ବାହାରିଲୁ) and keeps the tense for the last verb, with **ଯଦିଓ … ତଥାପି**, **ଫଳରେ**, **ଏପରିକି** and **କିମ୍ବା** to hold long thoughts together. Second, **switching register** mid-conversation — knowing who gets ଆପଣ, who gets ତୁମେ and who gets ତୁ, and changing your verbs, words and even your English as you turn from one person to another. The dialogue is the longest in the course: a trip to plan, a friendly fight, and a grandmother with a story.

grammar.title: Linking long sentences
grammar.body:
In real conversation Odia speakers string several actions and ideas into one long sentence. The key rule: **only the last verb carries tense and person**; every earlier verb goes into a **linking form**.

**One action after another**: **-ଇ** 'having done, and then' (unit 22): ସକାଳେ ଉଠି, ଚା ପିଇ, ଆମେ ବାହାରିଲୁ 'we got up, had tea and set off'. Spoken Odia also uses **-ଇକରି** (ପହଞ୍ଚିକରି) with the same meaning.

**Time**: **-ବା ପରେ** 'after', **-ବା ଆଗରୁ** 'before', **-ବା ବେଳେ** 'while' (unit 30), **-ଲେ** 'when / if'.

**Purpose**: **-ବା ପାଇଁ** 'in order to': ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟୋଦୟ ଦେଖିବା ପାଇଁ ପାଞ୍ଚଟାରେ ବାହାରିଲୁ.

**Reason and result**: reason + **ବୋଲି** / noun + **ଯୋଗୁଁ** 'because (of)'; result: **ସେଥିପାଇଁ**, **ତେଣୁ**, **ଫଳରେ** 'so, as a result'.

**Concession**: **ଯଦିଓ** … **ତଥାପି** 'although … still': ଯଦିଓ ବର୍ଷା ହେଉଥିଲା, ତଥାପି ଆମେ ଗଲୁ.

**Adding a surprise**: **ଏପରିକି** 'even': ସମସ୍ତେ ହସିଲେ, ଏପରିକି ଜେଜେ ବି.

**Alternatives**: **କିମ୍ବା** 'or' in statements, **ନା** 'or' in questions: ଶନିବାର କିମ୍ବା ରବିବାର ଯିବା · ଶନିବାର ନା ରବିବାର?

A whole story in one breath: ଆମେ ପାଞ୍ଚଟାରେ ଉଠି, ଚା ପିଇ, ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟୋଦୟ ଦେଖିବା ପାଇଁ ସମୁଦ୍ର କୂଳକୁ ଗଲୁ, କିନ୍ତୁ ମେଘ ଯୋଗୁଁ କିଛି ଦେଖି ହେଲା ନାହିଁ.

The trap: don't conjugate every verb and glue them with ଆଉ like English 'and… and… and'. ମୁଁ ଉଠିଲି ଆଉ ଗାଧୋଇଲି ଆଉ ଖାଇଲି is understandable but sounds like a child's essay; say ମୁଁ ଉଠି, ଗାଧୋଇ, ଖାଇଲି.

grammar.title: Switching register mid-conversation
grammar.body:
Real conversations rarely stay at one level. At a family dinner you might speak to your grandfather, your mother, your little brother and a guest within a minute — and in Odia every verb shows the difference.

**Who gets what** (typical in Odisha; families vary):
**ଆପଣ** — grandparents, guests, in-laws, older relatives you don't see often, officials, anyone you've just met who's older: ଜେଜେ, ଆପଣ ଆଉ କିଛି **ନେବେ**? Commands -ନ୍ତୁ: ବସ**ନ୍ତୁ**.
**ତୁମେ** — parents in many families, close aunts and uncles, colleagues and acquaintances your age: ବୋଉ, ତୁମେ ବି **ବସ**.
**ତୁ** — siblings, cousins, close friends, children: ଭାଇ, ଲୁଣ ଟିକେ **ଦେ** ତ!

**Talking *about* someone**: an elder keeps the respectful plural even when absent: ଜେଜେ **ଶୋଇଛନ୍ତି** (not ଶୋଇଛି), ଜେଜେ**ଙ୍କ** ଔଷଧ.

**Words shift too**: formal **ଭୋଜନ** / everyday ଖାଇବା; **ମଧ୍ୟ** / ବି; **ଆଜ୍ଞା** / ହଁ; କ୍ଷମା କରନ୍ତୁ / ସରି. With elders, use fewer English words and drop ରେ, ଧେତ୍, ଆରେ.

**Switching within one breath** is completely normal: ଭାଇ, ଶୀଘ୍ର ଆ — ଜେଜେ, ଆପଣ ବସନ୍ତୁ, ମୁଁ ପରଷୁଛି.

**Moving down a level is the elder's call**: if an older person tells you ମୋତେ ତୁମେ ବୋଲି କୁହ 'call me ତୁମେ', switch; never drop to ତୁ on your own.

The trap: mixing levels inside one address — ~~ଆପଣ ଆସ~~ or ~~ତୁମେ ଆସନ୍ତୁ~~ — sounds wrong. Choose the pronoun first, then make every verb match it.

dialogue.title: Where shall we go?
dialogue.setting: Rohan's family home in Cuttack, a Sunday afternoon. Rohan, Puja and Debu, friends since school, are planning a trip for the December holidays. Later Rohan's grandmother joins them.

lines.speaker: Puja
lines.native: ଶୁଣ, ଡିସେମ୍ବରରେ ତିନି ଦିନ ଛୁଟି ଅଛି। ଚାଲ, କୁଆଡ଼େ ବୁଲିଯିବା!
lines.roman: suṇô, ḍisembôrôre tini dinô chhuṭi ôchhi. chalô, kuaṛe bulijiba!
lines.en: Listen, we've got three days off in December. Let's go somewhere!

lines.speaker: Debu
lines.native: ଦାରିଙ୍ଗବାଡ଼ି! ଶୀତରେ ସେଠି ଏପରିକି ବରଫ ବି ପଡ଼େ ବୋଲି ଶୁଣିଛି।
lines.roman: Daringbaṛi! sitôre seṭhi epôriki bôrôphô bi pôṛe boli suṇichhi.
lines.en: Daringbadi! I've heard it even gets frost there in winter.

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.native: ଧେତ୍, ସେଠିକୁ ଯିବାକୁ ଆଠ ଘଣ୍ଟା ଲାଗିବ। ବରଂ ପୁରୀ ଯାଇ, କୋଣାର୍କରେ ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟୋଦୟ ଦେଖି, ଫେରିଆସିବା।
lines.roman: dhet, seṭhiku jibaku aṭhô ghôṇṭa lagibô. bôrôṅ Puri jai, Koṇarkôre surjyodôyô dekhi, pheriasiba.
lines.en: Come off it, it's eight hours to get there. Let's just go to Puri, watch the sunrise at Konark and come back.

lines.speaker: Puja
lines.native: ପୁରୀ? ଆମେ ପ୍ରତି ବର୍ଷ ପୁରୀ ଯାଉ! ତୁ ଜିଦ୍ କରୁଛୁ, ରୋହନ।
lines.roman: Puri? ame prôti bôrsô Puri jau! tu jid kôruchhu, Rohôn.
lines.en: Puri? We go to Puri every year! You're being stubborn, Rohan.

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.native: ମୁଁ ସିନା ଜିଦ୍ କରୁଛି, ହେଲେ ବଜେଟ୍ କଥା କିଏ ଭାବୁଛି?
lines.roman: muṃ sina jid kôruchhi, hele bôjeṭ kôtha kie bhabuchhi?
lines.en: Fine, *I'm* the stubborn one — but who's thinking about the budget?

lines.speaker: Debu
lines.native: ଆଚ୍ଛା, ମଝାମଝି କିଛି କରିବା। ଚିଲିକା କେମିତି? ବେଶି ଦୂର ନୁହେଁ, ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ବି କମ, ଆଉ ଡଲଫିନ୍ ଦେଖିବାକୁ ମିଳିବ।

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.native: ଆରେ, ଜେଜେମା ଆସିଲେ। ଜେଜେମା, ଆପଣ ଏଠି ବସନ୍ତୁ।

lines.roman: kôṇô gôpôsôpô chalichhi? mote bi kuhô.

lines.speaker: Puja

lines.roman: jejema, ame Chilika jiba kôtha bhabuchhu. apôṇô kebe jaichhônti ki?
lines.en: Grandma, we're thinking of going to Chilika. Have you ever been?

lines.speaker: Grandma
lines.native: ଯାଇଛି ତ! ବାହାଘର ପରେ ରୋହନର ଜେଜେଙ୍କ ସହ ଡଙ୍ଗାରେ ବୁଲିଥିଲି। ସେ ସ୍ମୃତି ଏବେ ବି ମନେ ଅଛି।

lines.en: Of course I have! After our wedding I went out on a boat with Rohan's grandfather. I still remember it.

lines.speaker: Debu
lines.native: ବାପରେ, କେତେ ରୋମାଣ୍ଟିକ୍! ଜେଜେମା, ଆପଣ ବି ଆମ ସହ ଚାଲନ୍ତୁ!
lines.roman: bapôre, kete romanṭik! jejema, apôṇô bi amô sôhô chalôntu!
lines.en: Wow, how romantic! Grandma, you come with us too!

lines.speaker: Grandma
lines.native: ହା ହା, ମୋ ଆଣ୍ଠୁ ଆଉ ଡଙ୍ଗା ସହିବ ନାହିଁ। ତୁମେମାନେ ଆଗୁଆ ବୁକ୍ କରି ଭଲରେ ଯାଅ, ପହଞ୍ଚିଲେ ଫୋନ କରିବ।
lines.roman: ha ha, mo aṇṭhu au ḍôṅga sôhibô nahiṃ. tumemane agua buk kôri bhôlôre jaô, pôhôñchile phonô kôribô.
lines.en: Ha ha, my knees can't take a boat any more. You book ahead and go safely, and phone when you get there.

lines.speaker: Rohan
lines.native: ଆଜ୍ଞା ଜେଜେମା। ହଉ, ପକ୍କା — ଚିଲିକା! ଭାଇମାନେ, ଏଥର ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ସମସ୍ତେ ମିଶି ଦେବା, ହଁ?
lines.roman: agya jejema. hôu, pôkka — Chilika! bhaimane, ethôrô khôrchchô sômôste misi deba, hôṃ?
lines.en: Yes, Grandma. Right, it's settled — Chilika! And guys, this time we all split the cost, OK?

culture:
A family meal in Odisha is the best place to hear every register at once. Food is served — often by the women of the house, though younger men increasingly help — with the eldest served first; guests are pressed to take more (**ଆଉ ଟିକେ ନିଅନ୍ତୁ**), and saying no once is just politeness. The menu is likely to include rice, **ଡାଲମା**, a fry (*bhaja*), some fish curry in coastal homes, and *pakhala* on hot days. Elders are **ଆପଣ** and are spoken *about* in the respectful plural; parents are **ତୁମେ** in many families and **ଆପଣ** in some; siblings and cousins are **ତୁ**, whatever their age gap. Touching an elder's feet (**ପ୍ରଣାମ**) when you arrive or before a journey earns a blessing — and probably a question about when you're getting married.

Odia friends plan trips loudly and lovingly: a friendly argument (**ମତଭେଦ**) is part of the fun, and **ସିନା** and **ଧେତ୍** fly around. Popular weekend escapes from Bhubaneswar and Cuttack include **Puri** and **Konark** on the coast, **Chilika** lake with its Irrawaddy dolphins and migratory birds in winter, the hills of **Daringbadi** in Kandhamal ('the Kashmir of Odisha'), and the forests of Simlipal. Costs are usually split equally among friends, often settled by UPI on the way home.

Finally, the send-off: whoever's travelling will hear **ଭଲରେ ଯିବ, ପହଞ୍ଚିଲେ ଫୋନ କରିବ** from every elder in the house. Say **ଆଜ୍ଞା** — and do call.

lessons.title: Catching up with an old friend

tip.title: Long time no see
tip.body:
- Greet: **ବହୁଦିନ ପରେ ଦେଖା!** · ତୁ ଜମା **ବଦଳିନୁ**!
- Remember together: **ତୋର ମନେ ଅଛି?** + what you used to do (-ଉଥିଲୁ).
- 'It's been ages since…': **ବହୁଦିନ ହେଲା** …
- Part warmly: **ଆଉ ଦିନେ ଗପସପ ହେବା**.

sentences.native: ବହୁଦିନ ପରେ ଦେଖା! କେମିତି ଅଛୁ?
sentences.roman: bôhudinô pôre dekha! kemiti ôchhu?
sentences.en: Long time no see! How are you?

sentences.native: ତୁ ଜମା ବଦଳିନୁ, ସେଇ ପୁରୁଣା ହସ!
sentences.roman: tu jôma bôdôḷinu, sei puruṇa hôsô!
sentences.en: You haven't changed a bit — the same old smile!

sentences.native: ତୋର ମନେ ଅଛି, ଆମେ କଲେଜରେ ଘଣ୍ଟା ଘଣ୍ଟା ଗପସପ କରୁଥିଲୁ?
sentences.roman: torô mône ôchhi, ame kôlejôre ghôṇṭa ghôṇṭa gôpôsôpô kôruthilu?
sentences.en: Remember how we used to chat for hours at college?

sentences.native: ସେ ସବୁ ସ୍ମୃତି ଏବେ ବି ମନେ ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: se sôbu smruti ebe bi mône ôchhi.
sentences.en: I still remember all of that.

sentences.native: ବହୁଦିନ ହେଲା ତୋ ସହ କଥା ହୋଇନି।
sentences.roman: bôhudinô hela to sôhô kôtha hoini.
sentences.en: It's been ages since we talked.

sentences.native: ଆଜି ସମୟ କମ, ଆଉ ଦିନେ ବସି ଗପସପ ହେବା।
sentences.roman: aji sômôyô kômô, au dine bôsi gôpôsôpô heba.
sentences.en: Not much time today — let's sit down and have a proper chat another day.

sentences.native: ଆଉ କ'ଣ ଖବର? ଘରେ ସମସ୍ତେ ଭଲ ତ?
sentences.roman: au kôṇô khôbôrô? ghôre sômôste bhôlô tô?
sentences.en: What's new? Everyone at home well?

sentences.native: ଫୋନ ନମ୍ବର ଦେ, ଏଥର ଯୋଗାଯୋଗ ରଖିବା।
sentences.roman: phonô nômbôrô de, ethôrô jogajogô rôkhiba.
sentences.en: Give me your number — let's keep in touch this time.

lessons.title: Telling it all in one breath

tip.title: Link, then finish
tip.body:
- Earlier verbs in **-ଇ**: ଉଠି, ଚା ପିଇ, … only the **last** verb takes tense: ବାହାରିଲୁ.
- Purpose **-ବା ପାଇଁ**; after **-ବା ପରେ**.
- **ଯଦିଓ … ତଥାପି** 'although … still' · **ଫଳରେ** 'as a result' · **ଏପରିକି** 'even' · **କିମ୍ବା** 'or'.

sentences.native: ସକାଳେ ଉଠି, ଚା ପିଇ, ଆମେ ସମୁଦ୍ର କୂଳକୁ ଗଲୁ।
sentences.roman: sôkaḷe uṭhi, cha pii, ame sômudrô kuḷôku gôlu.
sentences.en: We got up early, had tea and went to the beach.

sentences.native: ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟୋଦୟ ଦେଖିବା ପାଇଁ ଆମେ ପାଞ୍ଚଟାରେ ବାହାରିଲୁ।
sentences.roman: surjyodôyô dekhiba paiṃ ame pañchôṭare baharilu.
sentences.en: We set off at five to see the sunrise.

sentences.native: ମେଘ ଥିଲା, ଫଳରେ ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟୋଦୟ ଦେଖି ହେଲା ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: meghô thila, phôḷôre surjyodôyô dekhi hela nahiṃ.
sentences.en: It was cloudy, so we couldn't see the sunrise.

sentences.native: ଯଦିଓ ମୁଁ କ୍ଲାନ୍ତ ଥିଲି, ତଥାପି ପାର୍ଟିକୁ ଗଲି।
sentences.roman: jôdio muṃ klantô thili, tôthapi parṭiku gôli.
sentences.en: Even though I was tired, I still went to the party.

sentences.native: ସମସ୍ତେ ଓଦା ହୋଇଗଲେ, ଏପରିକି ମୋ ଫୋନ ବି।
sentences.roman: sômôste oda hoigôle, epôriki mo phonô bi.
sentences.en: Everyone got soaked — even my phone.

sentences.native: ଶନିବାର କିମ୍ବା ରବିବାର, ଯେଉଁ ଦିନ ତୁମେ ଫ୍ରି।
sentences.roman: sônibarô kimba rôbibarô, jeuṃ dinô tume phri.
sentences.en: Saturday or Sunday — whichever day you're free.

sentences.native: ଅଫିସରୁ ଫେରିବା ପରେ, ଖାଇ, ଟିକେ ଶୋଇ, ମୁଁ ସଞ୍ଜରେ ଆସିବି।
sentences.roman: ôphisôru pheriba pôre, khai, ṭike soi, muṃ sôñjôre asibi.
sentences.en: After work I'll eat, have a little nap, and come over in the evening.

sentences.native: ଟିକଟ ମିଳିଲା ନାହିଁ, ଫଳରେ ଆମେ ବସରେ ଗଲୁ।
sentences.roman: ṭikôṭô miḷila nahiṃ, phôḷôre ame bôsôre gôlu.
sentences.en: We couldn't get train tickets, so we went by bus.

sentences.native: ଆମେ ସାରା ଦିନ ବୁଲି, ମାଛ ଖାଇ, ରାତିରେ ଫେରିଲୁ।
sentences.roman: ame sara dinô buli, machhô khai, ratire pherilu.
sentences.en: We wandered around all day, had fish, and came back at night.

lessons.title: Planning a trip together

tip.title: Trip talk
tip.body:
- Money: **ବଜେଟ୍ କେତେ?** · ଜଣ ପିଛା **ମୋଟାମୋଟି** … · **ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ** ସମସ୍ତେ ମିଶି ଦେବା.
- Booking: **ଆଗୁଆ** ବୁକ୍ କରିନେବା; **ହୋମଷ୍ଟେ** or ହୋଟେଲ.
- 'Let's…': ଚାଲ + -ବା (ବାହାରିବା, କିଣିବା).
- Seeing someone off: **ଭଲରେ ଯିବ, ପହଞ୍ଚିଲେ ଫୋନ କରିବ**.

new: ଆଗୁଆ ବୁକ୍ କରିନେବା, ନହେଲେ ଜାଗା ମିଳିବ ନାହିଁ।

sentences.native: ଜଣ ପିଛା ବଜେଟ୍ ମୋଟାମୋଟି ପାଞ୍ଚ ହଜାର।
sentences.roman: jôṇô pichha bôjeṭ moṭamoṭi pañchô hôjarô.
sentences.en: The budget's roughly five thousand per person.

sentences.native: ହୋମଷ୍ଟେରେ ରହିଲେ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ କମ ହେବ।
sentences.roman: homsṭere rôhile khôrchchô kômô hebô.
sentences.en: If we stay in a homestay, it'll cost less.

sentences.native: ଛୁଟି ଦିନ ଭିଡ଼ ହେବ, ଆଗୁଆ ଟିକଟ କିଣିବା।
sentences.roman: chhuṭi dinô bhiṛô hebô, agua ṭikôṭô kiṇiba.
sentences.en: It'll be crowded over the holiday — let's buy tickets in advance.

sentences.native: ହୋମଷ୍ଟେ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ମୁଁ ଦେବି, ଖାଇବା ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ତୁମେମାନେ ଦିଅ।
sentences.roman: homsṭe khôrchchô muṃ debi, khaiba khôrchchô tumemane diô.
sentences.en: I'll pay for the homestay, you lot pay for the food.

sentences.native: ଆମେ ମୋଟାମୋଟି ସକାଳ ଛଅଟାରେ ବାହାରିବା।
sentences.roman: ame moṭamoṭi sôkaḷô chhôṭare bahariba.
sentences.en: We'll leave at around six in the morning.

sentences.native: ଭଲରେ ଯିବ, ଆଉ ପହଞ୍ଚିଲେ ଫୋନ କରିବ, ହଁ?
sentences.roman: bhôlôre jibô, au pôhôñchile phonô kôribô, hôṃ?
sentences.en: Travel safely, and call when you get there, OK?

sentences.native: ବଜେଟ୍ ଟିକେ ବଢ଼ାଇଲେ ଭଲ ହୋଟେଲ ମିଳିବ।
sentences.roman: bôjeṭ ṭike bôṛhaile bhôlô hoṭelô miḷibô.
sentences.en: If we stretch the budget a bit, we'll get a nice hotel.

sentences.native: ଫେରିଲେ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଭାଗ କରିବା।
sentences.roman: pherile khôrchchô sômôstôṅkô môdhyôre bhagô kôriba.
sentences.en: When we're back we'll split the costs between everyone.

lessons.title: Arguing it out

tip.title: A friendly fight
tip.body:
- Accuse: ତୁ **ଜିଦ୍** କରୁଛୁ! · Fight back: ମୁଁ **ସିନା** ଜିଦ୍ କରୁଛି, ହେଲେ …
- Stay on track: **ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗ ବଦଳାଅ ନାହିଁ!**
- Compromise: **ମଝାମଝି** କିଛି ଠିକ୍ କରିବା · ଚାଲ ଭୋଟ୍ କରିବା.
- Fairness: **ଏଥର ମୋ ପାଳି** · ସେ ପ୍ଲାନ୍ **ବାଦ୍ ଦିଅ**.

new: ଜିଦ୍ କର ନାହିଁ, ମଝାମଝି କିଛି ଠିକ୍ କରିବା।

sentences.native: ଆମ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଟିକେ ମତଭେଦ ଅଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଝଗଡ଼ା ନୁହେଁ।
sentences.roman: amô môdhyôre ṭike môtôbhedô ôchhi, kintu jhôgôṛa nuheṃ.
sentences.en: We disagree a bit, but it's not a fight.

sentences.native: ତୁ ସବୁବେଳେ ଜିଦ୍ କରୁ!
sentences.roman: tu sôbubeḷe jid kôru!
sentences.en: You're always so stubborn!

sentences.native: ଗତ ଥର ତୁମ କଥା ମାନିଲୁ, ଏଥର ମୋ ପାଳି।
sentences.roman: gôtô thôrô tumô kôtha manilu, ethôrô mo paḷi.
sentences.en: Last time we went along with you — this time it's my turn.

sentences.native: ମଝାମଝି ଗୋଟେ ଜାଗା ଖୋଜିବା, ଯେଉଁଠି ପାହାଡ଼ ବି ଅଛି, ନଦୀ ବି ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: môjhamôjhi goṭe jaga khojiba, jeuṃṭhi pahaṛô bi ôchhi, nôdi bi ôchhi.
sentences.en: Let's find somewhere in between, with hills and a river.

sentences.native: ସେ ପ୍ଲାନ୍ ବାଦ୍ ଦିଅ, ବହୁତ ଦୂର।
sentences.roman: se plan bad diô, bôhutô durô.
sentences.en: Drop that plan — it's too far.

sentences.native: ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗ ବଦଳାଅ ନାହିଁ, ଆଗେ କୁହ କେଉଁଠି ଯିବା।
sentences.roman: prôsôṅgô bôdôḷaô nahiṃ, age kuhô keuṃṭhi jiba.
sentences.en: Don't change the subject — first tell me where we're going.

sentences.native: ଜିଦ୍ କର ନାହିଁ, ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ କଥା ଶୁଣ।
sentences.roman: jid kôrô nahiṃ, sômôstôṅkô kôtha suṇô.
sentences.en: Don't be stubborn — listen to everyone.

sentences.native: ତୁମ ଦୁଇ ଜଣଙ୍କ ମତ ଅଲଗା, ଚାଲ ଭୋଟ୍ କରିବା।
sentences.roman: tumô dui jôṇôṅkô môtô ôlôga, chalô bhoṭ kôriba.
sentences.en: You two don't agree — let's vote.

sentences.native: ପାଳି କରି ଗାଡ଼ି ଚଳାଇବା, ଜଣେ ଏକୁଟିଆ ଚଳାଇଲେ ଥକିଯିବ।
sentences.roman: paḷi kôri gaṛi chôḷaiba, jôṇe ekuṭia chôḷaile thôkijibô.
sentences.en: Let's take turns driving — one person on their own will get worn out.

tip.title: ଆପଣ, ତୁମେ, ତୁ — at one table
tip.body:
- Grandparents, guests: **ଆପଣ** + -ନ୍ତୁ / -ବେ: ଜେଜେ, ବସନ୍ତୁ.
- Parents (often): **ତୁମେ** + bare verb: ବୋଉ, ବସ.
- Siblings, friends: **ତୁ** + stem: ଭାଇ, ଆଣ୍ ତ!
- About an elder: respectful plural — ଜେଜେମା ଖାଇଛ**ନ୍ତି**. Formal words: **ଭୋଜନ, ମଧ୍ୟ**.
tip.pattern: pick the pronoun → match every verb

sentences.native: ଜେଜେ, ଆପଣ ଆଗେ ବସନ୍ତୁ, ମୁଁ ପରଷୁଛି।
sentences.roman: jeje, apôṇô age bôsôntu, muṃ pôrôsuchhi.
sentences.en: Grandpa, you sit down first — I'll serve.

sentences.native: ବୋଉ, ତୁମେ ବି ଆସି ବସ, ସବୁବେଳେ କାମ!
sentences.roman: bou, tume bi asi bôsô, sôbubeḷe kamô!
sentences.en: Mum, you come and sit down too — always working!

sentences.native: ଭାଇ, ପାଣି ଗିଲାସଟା ଆଣ୍ ତ!
sentences.roman: bhai, paṇi gilasôṭa aṇ tô!
sentences.en: Bro, grab the glass of water, will you!

sentences.native: ଆଜିର ଡାଲମା ବହୁତ ସୁଆଦିଆ ହୋଇଛି।
sentences.roman: ajirô ḍalma bôhutô suadia hoichhi.
sentences.en: The dalma's turned out delicious today.

sentences.native: ଆପଣଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ଆଉ ଟିକେ ଭାତ ପରଷିବି?
sentences.roman: apôṇôṅkô paiṃ au ṭike bhatô pôrôsibi?
sentences.en: Shall I serve you a bit more rice?

sentences.native: ଆମ ସମ୍ପର୍କୀୟମାନେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଭୋଜନରେ ଯୋଗ ଦେବେ।
sentences.roman: amô sômpôrkiyômane môdhyô bhojônôre jogô debe.
sentences.en: Our relatives will also be joining us for the meal.

sentences.native: ଜେଜେମା ଔଷଧ ଖାଇଛନ୍ତି କି?
sentences.roman: jejema ôusôdhô khaichhônti ki?
sentences.en: Has Grandma taken her medicine?

sentences.native: ଭୋଜନ ପାଇଁ ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ, ମାଉସୀ।
sentences.roman: bhojônô paiṃ dhônnyôbadô, mausi.
sentences.en: Thank you for the meal, auntie.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଆପଣଙ୍କ ସହ ଏକମତ।
sentences.roman: muṃ môdhyô apôṇôṅkô sôhô ekômôtô.
sentences.en: I agree with you too.
